mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The threat for severe weather is expected to increase this morning, likely necessitating a watch issuance

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for severe weather is expected to increase this morning, likely necessitating a watch issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A gradual increase in thunderstorms, including splitting supercell structures, has been observed over northwest IN over the past hour or so. That activity appears to be associated with a zone of warm advection occurring to the north of an outflow boundary extending from west-central through southeast IN. Regional 12Z soundings sampled a strongly unstable environment in place this morning, which is likely to sustain the ongoing storms with some large hail and locally damaging wind potential. A greater severe weather threat, mainly in the form of damaging winds with significant gusts, is expected to move into the area from the northwest in association with a bowing MCS ongoing across north-central IL

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The potential for significant wind gusts up to 75-85 mph is expected to persist with an evolving bow echo this morning

details.label: Summary
details.text: The potential for significant wind gusts up to 75-85 mph is expected to persist with an evolving bow echo this morning

details.label: Discussion
details.text: An MCS with a history of producing wind gusts of 70-80 mph is currently evolving into a broader bowing configuration over east-central IA and far northwest IL as of 1355Z. The 12z DVN sounding is likely a good representation of the ambient inflow environment, featuring steep mid-level lapse rates and abundant boundary-layer moisture, yielding MUCAPE of 4500-5000 J/kg. A largely unidirectional wind profile with around 35 kt of deep-layer shear (per the 12z DVN sounding and current VWP) in conjunction with the strongly unstable environment is likely to support further intensification of the bow echo with an associated risk for significant wind gusts up to 75-85 mph. Around 30 kt of 0-3 km shear oriented largely perpendicular to the cold pool may support some tornado potential, especially where the low-level shear and cold pool remain in balance. The bow echo is expected to track along a residual outflow boundary from a downstream MCS, which extends east-southeast through the south side of the greater Chicago metropolitan area into far northwest IN
